verses.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचभूय एव महाबाहो श्रृणु मे परमं वचः । यत्तेऽहं प्रीयमाणाय वक्ष्यामि हितकाम्यया ॥
verses.tr: The Blessed Lord says: Listen again, O mighty-armed one, to my supreme word, which I will speak for your welfare because you are deeply dear to me.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna turns to what comes next, asking Arjuna to listen once more.

body.text: The Blessed Lord says: Listen again, O mighty-armed one, to my supreme word, which I will speak for your welfare because you are deeply dear to me. Krishna opens chapter ten by telling Arjuna he speaks again because Arjuna is dear to him. Krishna now says even the great sages do not know his origin, and he is the source of them all.

verses.sa: न मे विदुः सुरगणाः प्रभवं न महर्षयः । अहमादिर्हि देवानां महर्षीणां च सर्वशः ॥
verses.tr: The hosts of devas do not know my origin, nor do the great sages, for I am the beginning of the devas and the great sages in every way.
verses.angle: Origin unknown to devas and sages
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: If the great sages and the hosts of gods do not know Krishna's source, what exactly is this origin he speaks of? Listen for the answer.

body.text: The hosts of devas do not know my origin, nor do the great sages, for I am the beginning of the devas and the great sages in every way. The hosts of devas and great sages do not know my origin. Krishna states that even these exalted beings cannot trace his source, because he is the very beginning of all of them. Krishna then says that whoever knows him as unborn and without beginning is freed from all wrong deeds.

verses.sa: यो मामजमनादिं च वेत्ति लोकमहेश्वरम् । असम्मूढः स मर्त्येषु सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
verses.tr: One who knows Me as unborn, beginningless, and the great lord of all worlds is undeluded among mortals and is freed from every wrong deed.
verses.angle: Asammudhah: freed from all wrong deeds
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just said that even the gods and sages do not know his origin. Now he tells the listener what happens when they do know him.

body.text: One who knows Me as unborn, beginningless, and the great lord of all worlds is undeluded among mortals and is freed from every wrong deed. The word asammudhah means undeluded, and the verse says that person is freed from all wrong deeds. Knowing Krishna as the beginningless lord of all worlds removes confusion and frees a person from wrongdoing. Krishna next lists the qualities that arise from him alone, starting with understanding and wisdom.

verses.sa: बुद्धिर्ज्ञानमसंमोहः क्षमा सत्यं दमः शमः । सुखं दुःखं भवोऽभावो भयं चाभयमेव च ॥
verses.tr: Understanding, wisdom, freedom from confusion, forgiveness, truth, self-restraint, calmness, pleasure, pain, coming into being, ceasing to be, fear, fearlessness, nonviolence, evenness, contentment, austerity, charity, fame, and disgrace arise from me alone.
verses.angle: Bhayam and abhayameva, both from the same source
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: In this verse, Krishna lists the conditions of human life. Listen for the two words that sit together at the end, bhayam and abhayameva.

body.text: Understanding, wisdom, freedom from confusion, forgiveness, truth, self-restraint, calmness, pleasure, pain, coming into being, ceasing to be, fear, fearlessness, nonviolence, evenness, contentment, austerity, charity, fame, and disgrace arise from me alone. Krishna puts bhayam, fear, and abhayameva, fearlessness, in the same breath. He does not say that fearlessness is the end of fear; he says both are his. Next, Krishna says that nonviolence, honor, and dishonor all arise from him alone.

verses.sa: अहिंसा समता तुष्टिस्तपो दानं यशोऽयशः । भवन्ति भावा भूतानां मत्त एव पृथग्विधाः ॥
verses.tr: Nonviolence, equanimity, contentment, austerity, charity, honor, and dishonor, all these different states of beings arise from Me alone.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna tells Arjuna that nonviolence, balance, contentment, discipline, generosity, honor, and dishonor all arise from him alone. Listen to how he frames these qualities.

body.text: Nonviolence, equanimity, contentment, austerity, charity, honor, and dishonor, all these different states of beings arise from Me alone. Krishna lists honor and dishonor side by side. Both are states of beings that arise from him alone. Krishna then says that even the great sages and Manus were born from his mind.

verses.sa: महर्षयः सप्त पूर्वे चत्वारो मनवस्तथा । मद्भावा मानसा जाता येषां लोक इमाः प्रजाः ॥
verses.tr: The seven great sages, the four ancient sages, and the fourteen Manus were born from my mind. The people of these worlds descend from them.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna widens Arjuna’s sight from the battlefield to the source of all life. Listen for the origin he names here.

body.text: The seven great sages, the four ancient sages, and the fourteen Manus were born from my mind. The people of these worlds descend from them. The sages and Manus did not arrive as bodies from outside; they were born from his mind, and every person in the world descends through that single line of thought. Krishna then tells Arjuna that knowing this truth makes one stand firm in yoga without any doubt.

verses.sa: एतां विभूतिं योगं च मम यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः । सोऽविकम्पेन योगेन युज्यते नात्र संशयः ॥
verses.tr: One who truly knows this glory and this yoga of mine becomes steadfast in yoga without doubt.
verses.angle: Tattvatah: knowing in truth removes doubt
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just listed the signs of his presence. Now he tells Arjuna what happens to someone who truly understands them.

body.text: One who truly knows this glory and this yoga of mine becomes steadfast in yoga without doubt. Listen for the word tattvatah, knowing in truth. It is not mere learning, but a deep realization that makes the mind unshaken and removes all doubt. Krishna then adds that he is the source of all and that everything moves from him.

verses.sa: अहं सर्वस्य प्रभवो मत्तः सर्वं प्रवर्तते । इति मत्वा भजन्ते मां बुधा भावसमन्विताः ॥
verses.tr: I am the source of all; everything moves from me. Knowing this, the wise worship me with wholehearted devotion.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has shown his many forms. Now he says where they all come from. Listen to who moves and what the wise do.

body.text: I am the source of all; everything moves from me. Knowing this, the wise worship me with wholehearted devotion. Notice the word matatah, from me. Everything that exists, Krishna says, moves and proceeds from him. The wise, knowing this, worship me with wholehearted devotion.

verses.sa: मच्चित्ता मद्गतप्राणा बोधयन्तः परस्परम् । कथयन्तश्च मां नित्यं तुष्यन्ति च रमन्ति च ॥
verses.tr: With minds fixed on Me and lives offered to Me, My devotees speak of Me to one another, and find continual joy in that shared devotion.
verses.angle: paratahparam: one another and shared joy
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna points to one word that shows how his followers find their joy together, through shared talk. Listen for it.

body.text: With minds fixed on Me and lives offered to Me, My devotees speak of Me to one another, and find continual joy in that shared devotion. Listen to paratahparam, meaning one another. The devotees speak of Krishna to each other, and that shared conversation is what makes them find continual joy. Krishna then offers the gift of discernment to those who are always devoted and worship him with love.

verses.sa: तेषां सततयुक्तानां भजतां प्रीतिपूर्वकम् । ददामि बुद्धियोगं तं येन मामुपयान्ति ते ॥
verses.tr: To those who are always devoted and worship Me with love, I give the discernment that leads them to Me.
verses.angle: buddhi-yoga, the discernment that leads to him
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna turns the talk from devotion to wisdom, promising a gift to those who love him steadily. Listen for what he gives and to whom.

body.text: To those who are always devoted and worship Me with love, I give the discernment that leads them to Me. Notice that the gift here is not a weapon or a sign, but buddhi-yoga, the discernment that leads to him. Krishna gives the mind that can find him to those who keep worshipping with steady love. This gift of discernment is not limited to the battlefield; it is a light that destroys ignorance within the devotee's own self.

verses.tr: To show them compassion, I destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the shining lamp of knowledge, dwelling in their own being.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues explaining how he helps his devotees. Listen closely to the two images he uses.

body.text: To show them compassion, I destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the shining lamp of knowledge, dwelling in their own being. Notice the word anukampartham, for compassion. Krishna does not destroy ignorance because it is wrong to be ignorant, but because he pities the one who is lost in it. Arjuna now speaks, and he lists the many names he gives to Krishna in his awe.
